Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThe patient\/ attender was informed the purpose of the information being acquired. An informed consent was taken from patient\/ attender and there is omission of information that was requested to be omitted.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;A 83yr old male came with complaints of\u0026nbsp; shortness of breath\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003Echief\u0026nbsp; complaints:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;cough since 14 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eshortness of breath since 10 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHistory of Presenting illness:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was admitted to ICU on 20\/11\/23 in the morning at 10 am with\u0026nbsp; breathlessness. It was insidious in onset and gradually progressive, continuous and present during rest ( patient\u0026nbsp; was feeling breathless even upon walking to washroom) with no associated relieving factors. Patient's attender also complained of awakening during night due to breathlessness. No h\/o palpitations, stridor, or hoarseness of voice\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient also complained of\u0026nbsp; cough which was insidious in onset, gradually progressive associated with sputum which was white in colour ,scanty\u0026nbsp; amount, mucoid in consistency and non foul smelling\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient also complained of intermittent spikes of fever\u0026nbsp; since 12 days( 4 times a day ), associated with chills and rigors, not relieved on taking medication and not associated with headache, vomiting\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;No h\/o chest pain, orthopnea, PND\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o recurrent sore throat or cold\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o loss of consciousness,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of similar complaints in the past\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is N\/K\/C\/O of Hypertension, Diabetes mellitus, TB, Epilepsy, Bronchial asthma, Thyroid disorders\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o blood transfusions and surgeries\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFAMILY HISTORY: \u003C\/b\u003EInsignificant\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of progressive weight loss since 6 months as mentioned by the attender\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet - Mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite - decreased\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep- Adequate\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and Bladder movements- Regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddiction - consumption of alcohol occasionally,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;h\/o smoking since 30 yrs (3 packs per day) reduced to 1 pack per day since 2 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EGENERAL EXAMINATION :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is unconscious.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe is moderately built\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is presence of pallor ,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003Epedal edema up to the knee\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(53, 53, 53); color: #353535; font-family: Merriweather, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; text-align: justify; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EBronchial breathing is the breath sound heard over the tracheobronchial tree. Bronchial breath sounds are loud, harsh breath sounds with midrange pitch and intensity. These sounds typically emanate from the larynx, trachea, and bronchi. The expiratory sound is longer than the inspiratory sound.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(53, 53, 53); color: #353535; font-family: Merriweather, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; text-align: justify; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Vesicular breathing is soft, low pitched, rustling in quality, while bronchial breathing is loud, harsh breath sounds with midrange pitch and intensity.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Semibold\u0026quot;\" style=\"font-weight: bold;\"\u003EBronchial breathing\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E anywhere other than over the trachea, right clavicle or right interscapular space is abnormal. Presence of bronchial breathing would suggest:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003EConsolidation \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003ECavitation \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003EComplete alveolar atelectasis with patent airways\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003EMass interposed between chest wall and large airways\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003ETension Pneumothorax\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System Font\u0026quot;; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;.SFUI-Regular\u0026quot;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003E•\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-tab-span\" style=\"white-space: pre;\"\u003E\t\u003C\/span\u003EMassive pleural effusion with complete atelectasis of lung\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.meddean.luc.edu\/lumen\/meded\/medicine\/pulmonar\/pd\/b-sounds.htm\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.meddean.luc.edu\/lumen\/meded\/medicine\/pulmonar\/pd\/b-sounds.htm\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #353535; font-family: Merriweather, Times New Roman, Times, serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(53, 53, 53); text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E3.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003EEtiopathogenesis of pneumonia.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: trebuchet; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003EThe most frequently isolated microorganisms were\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EP. aeruginosa\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;(n=9, 18%) and methicillin-resistant\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EStaphylococcus aureus\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;(MRSA; n=8, 16%). Positive blood cultures with agents considered as causative of pneumonia were found in six patients (\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EKlebsiella oxytoca, Enterobacter aerogenes, P. aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Enterobacter cloacae\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;and MRSA). Aetiological diagnosis of pleural empyema was achieved in three of five cases, and the causative agents were MRSA in two cases and coinfection of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EStreptococcus milleri\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;and\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EE. coli\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;in another case. Four patients with negative serum Aspergillus antigen had\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EAspergillus fumigatus\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; text-align: start; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;isolated in association with a Gram-negative strain and were not considered pathogenic. One patient submitted to surgical resection of lung aspergiloma developed a postoperative pneumonia with no other microorganism isolated besides Aspergillus, had a positive serum Aspergillus antigen, and therefore the fungus was considered the causative agent. Legionella urinary antigen was performed in 49% of patients, without any positive results.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.nhlbi.nih.gov\/health\/pneumonia\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.nhlbi.nih.gov\/health\/pneumonia\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EWhat sounds are typically heard in this case?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(31, 31, 31); color: #1f1f1f; font-family: ElsevierGulliver, Georgia, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, STIXGeneral, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Lucida Sans Unicode\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Microsoft Sans Serif\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Symbol\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Arial Unicode MS\u0026quot;, serif; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EGurgling sounds heard during tidal breathing or speech, or auscultated over the larynx, are strongly associated with HAP.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(31, 31, 31); color: #1f1f1f; font-family: ElsevierGulliver, Georgia, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, STIXGeneral, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Lucida Sans Unicode\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Microsoft Sans Serif\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI Symbol\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Arial Unicode MS\u0026quot;, serif; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003EIn very ill patients, gurgling is usually associated with severe debilitation or death. “Death rattle is a term applied to dying patients to describe the noise produced by the oscillatory movements of secretions in the upper airways.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/abs\/pii\/S0012369210604084\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Ca name='more'\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/abs\/pii\/S0012369210604084\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/abs\/pii\/S0012369210604084\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EFurther management of this case and role of ECMO\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E(extra corporeal membrane oxygenation).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; font-family: Aeonik, Arial, sans-serif; margin: 0px 0px 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003ETraditionally, lung\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 18px;\"\u003E failure is treated with mechanical ventilation, also called a breathing machine. These machines use positive pressure to push more air into the lungs and facilitate gas exchange, thus providing needed oxygen and removing carbon dioxide. The problem is that humans breathe naturally with a negative pressure breathing mechanism, so normally, when we inhale, the pressure in our lungs is negative, so breathing machines work the opposite of our normal breathing. For people who are very sick, this increase in positive pressure can strain the lungs by increasing the volume and pressure of air being inhaled, which in turn can cause lung injury. ECMO works because it allows the lungs to rest and it allows us to minimize the harm that the breathing machine causes.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; font-size: 18px; margin: 0px 0px 15px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EECMO pulls your blood outside of the body from one large vein, puts it through a pump which then pushes the blood through a membrane lung that facilitates gas exchange externally. It then returns your oxygenated blood to your body via another large vein through a tube that's positioned close to the right side of the heart. The ECMO machine performs the function of the lungs successfully so the lungs can rest and we can use very low settings on the breathing machine. This protects the lungs from additional damage that the high pressures from the breathing machine cause.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/erj.ersjournals.com\/content\/22\/6\/876\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/erj.ersjournals.com\/content\/22\/6\/876\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;System 70 year old female with vomitings "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis is an a online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThe patient\/ attender was informed the purpose of the information being acquired. An informed consent was taken from patient\/ attender and there is omission of information that was requested to be omitted.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChief complaints\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E70 year old female from narketpally housewife by occupation came with chief complaints of vomitings since 10 days generalized weakness since 10 days and pain abdomen associated with fever.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHOPI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 10 days back then she developed vomitings after comsuming food. Vomitus was non bilious non projectile, no hematemesis, watery in consistently food particles were present.
